name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
summary: A blue field with a yellow right triangle and a diagonal line of white stars, half-stars at each end. It was imposed in 1998 by the international High Representative, as the country's ethnic communities could not agree on a design.
origin: During the war of 1992–1995 the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina used a white flag with a blue shield of fleurs-de-lis, a symbol associated with Bosniaks and the medieval Kotromanić dynasty. Bosnian Serbs and Croats rejected it.

After the Dayton Agreement, the parliament failed to agree on a flag. High Representative Carlos Westendorp chose this design from several proposals, and it was introduced in time for the 1998 Winter Olympics in Nagano.

symbols.name: Triangle
symbols.description: A yellow right triangle near the hoist.
symbols.meaning: The rough shape of the country; its three points are often said to represent the three constituent peoples: Bosniaks, Croats and Serbs.

symbols.name: Stars
symbols.description: Seven full and two half white stars along the triangle's hypotenuse.
symbols.meaning: Europe; the stars are meant to continue infinitely, so they are cut off at the edges.

history.label: Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina
history.note: White with a blue shield of fleurs-de-lis.

facts: It is one of the few national flags chosen by an international official rather than the country itself.
Its blue and stars are deliberately reminiscent of the flag of the European Union.
The constituent entities, the Federation and Republika Srpska, have their own flags.
clues: A yellow triangle on blue with a diagonal line of white stars.
Chosen by an international official after local leaders could not agree.
Its triangle is said to show the shape of the country.
Its stars are cut off at the edges to suggest they continue forever.
